ambiguities.text: The specification says the wallet can 'arbitrarily refuse or accept the request' without defining what criteria might be used
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume wallet implementations have full discretion over acceptance criteria, but should prioritize user security and experience.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define how to handle pending transactions or confirmations during a chain switch
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume pending RPC requests and user confirmations for the old chain should be cancelled to prevent confusion.

ambiguities.text: The term 'active chain' is defined as 'the chain the wallet is forwarding RPC requests to' but doesn't address wallets with multiple simultaneous connections
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'active chain' refers to the primary/default chain context for the requesting dapp's session.

implicit_assumptions.description: Users understand the implications of switching chains, including that their displayed balance and assets may change
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Users may be confused or make mistakes when they see different balances after a chain switch

implicit_assumptions.description: The wallet can reliably identify the requesting dapp's origin and display it accurately to the user
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attackers could impersonate trusted dapps to trick users into switching to malicious chains

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot enumerate wallet chain support through timing attacks on rejection responses
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Wallet fingerprinting attacks could identify users across sessions based on supported chain set

implicit_assumptions.description: The wallet has valid, up-to-date RPC endpoints for all chains in its registry
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Chain switches could fail or connect to malicious endpoints if chain configuration is stale
